examples.en: It was so cold that people walked as slowly as grubs.

examples.ko: 피곤하면 저는 하루 종일 굼벵이가 돼요.
examples.en: When I'm tired, I turn into a slowpoke all day.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 흙 속에서 굼벵이를 처음 봤어요.
examples.en: When I was little, I saw a grub in the soil for the first time.

examples.ko: 매미 굼벵이는 땅속에서 오랫동안 살다가 나와요.
examples.en: Cicada larvae live underground for a long time before coming out.

examples.ko: 굼벵이 같은 동작 때문에 청소가 안 끝나요.
examples.en: Because of the snail-paced movements, the cleaning never ends.
What's the point of telling a slowpoke to run fast?

explain: 곤충의 애벌레를 가리키지만, 일상에서는 동작이 느리고 굼뜬 사람을 놀리는 비유로 더 자주 써요. 가까운 사이의 농담에는 괜찮지만 윗사람에게는 쓰지 않는 게 좋아요.

phrases.example: 굼벵이도 구르는 재주가 있다더니, 그 친구가 노래 대회에서 상을 받았어요.
phrases.en: Even a grub has the talent of rolling.
phrases.nuance_ko: 둔해 보이는 사람도 한 가지 재주는 있다는 뜻의 속담이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A proverb meaning even a seemingly dull person has some talent.

explain_en: It refers to an insect larva, but in daily life it is more often a teasing way to describe a slow, sluggish person. It's fine as a joke between close friends, but avoid using it about someone senior.

examples.en: I shape the dough into round balls and bake them.
The baby's cheeks are round and cute.
The stones by the river have been worn round.

examples.ko: 동글동글한 안경을 쓰면 인상이 부드러워 보여요.
examples.en: Wearing round glasses makes you look softer.
I packed the snow into round balls and made a snowman.

examples.ko: 접시에 동글동글 담긴 주먹밥이 맛있어 보여요.
examples.en: The round rice balls on the plate look delicious.

explain: 작고 귀여운 둥근 모양을 말할 때 써요. '동글동글하다'로도 쓰고, 더 큰 느낌이면 '둥글둥글'이라고 해요. 사람 성격이 모나지 않을 때는 '성격이 둥글둥글하다'라고 말해요.

phrases.en: There are small round cookies on the plate.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸밀 때 '동글동글한'으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '동글동글한' to describe a noun that follows.

phrases.en: I sliced the carrot into round pieces.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모양을 어떻게 만드는지 말할 때 '-게'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '-게' to say how something is shaped or cut.

phrases.en: The baby's face is round and cute.
phrases.nuance_ko: '동글동글하다'를 해요체로 바꿔서 모양을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite form of 동글동글하다, used to describe a round shape.

explain_en: It describes a small, cute round shape. It is also used as the adjective '동글동글하다', and the bigger-feeling version is '둥글둥글'. For an easygoing personality you say '성격이 둥글둥글하다'.

en: to be dull and heavy (of a sound)

examples.en: The sound of knocking on the door is a bit dull.

examples.ko: 무거운 가방이 바닥에 떨어지는 둔탁한 소리가 났어요.
examples.en: There was a dull thud of a heavy bag falling on the floor.

examples.ko: 이불 때문에 소리가 둔탁하게 들렸나 봐요.
examples.en: The sound probably came across muffled because of the blanket.
When I tapped the wall, it gave a dull sound.

examples.ko: 위층에서 둔탁한 쿵 소리가 계속 들려요.
examples.en: I keep hearing a dull thump from upstairs.

examples.ko: 문이 닫히는 소리가 둔탁해서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: The door closed with a heavy thud, and it startled me.

explain: '쿵', '퍽' 같은 무겁고 맑지 않은 소리를 말할 때 잘 어울려요. 반대로 맑고 높은 소리는 '맑다', '또렷하다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: A dull thud came from behind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에 붙는 가장 흔한 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common form before a noun.

phrases.en: This drum has a dull sound.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리가 맑지 않다는 평가를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Says that a sound is not clear.

phrases.en: The drum sounded dull and heavy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리가 낮고 무겁게 퍼질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a sound spreads low and heavy.

explain_en: It suits heavy, unclear sounds like '쿵' or '퍽'. For clear, high sounds, people say '맑다' or '또렷하다' instead.

t90.ax: I keep hearing a dull thump from upstairs.

en: to be tepid; to be lukewarm

examples.en: The coffee went cold and is lukewarm.

examples.ko: 뜨뜻미지근한 물로 샤워했더니 별로 개운하지 않았어요.
examples.en: I showered with lukewarm water and didn't feel very refreshed.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 일을 뜨뜻미지근하게 처리해서 답답해요.
examples.en: He handles work in a halfhearted way, which is frustrating.

examples.ko: 질문에 뜨뜻미지근하게 대답하지 말고 분명히 말해 주세요.
examples.en: Please don't answer vaguely; tell me clearly.

examples.ko: 회의 분위기가 뜨뜻미지근해서 결론이 안 났어요.
examples.en: The meeting atmosphere was lukewarm, so no conclusion was reached.
Please eat quickly before the soup turns lukewarm.

explain: 뜨겁지도 차갑지도 않은 어중간한 온도를 말해요. 비슷한 말은 '미지근하다'예요. 태도나 분위기가 분명하지 않고 열의가 없을 때 비유로도 자주 써요.

phrases.en: I washed my hands with lukewarm water.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ'을 붙여 어중간한 온도의 물을 꾸며 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-ㄴ' lets it describe water of in-between temperature.

phrases.en: The soup has cooled and is lukewarm.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금의 온도를 해요체로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite form for the current temperature.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 일에 뜨뜻미지근한 태도를 보였어요.
phrases.en: He showed a lukewarm attitude toward the work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 열의 없는 태도를 비유로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figurative use for a half-hearted attitude.

explain_en: It describes a halfway temperature that is neither hot nor cold. A similar word is '미지근하다'. It is also often used figuratively for an unclear, unenthusiastic attitude or atmosphere.

en: to be dull; to be prosaic; to be vapid

examples.ko: 매일 같은 일만 하니까 생활이 무미건조해요.
examples.en: I only do the same things every day, so my life feels dull.

examples.ko: 그 사람 말투가 너무 무미건조해서 재미가 없어요.
examples.en: His way of speaking is so dry that it's not fun.
Everyone dozed off because of the dull presentation.

examples.ko: 편지를 무미건조하게 써서 정이 안 느껴졌어요.
examples.en: The letter was written so drily that I couldn't feel any warmth.
My daily life feels dull these days.
He answered in a flat, emotionless voice.

explain: 말투, 글, 생활처럼 감정이나 재미가 느껴지지 않을 때 써요. '재미없다'보다 딱딱한 느낌이라 글이나 발표에서 더 자주 보여요. '무미건조한 + 명사', '무미건조하게 + 동사' 형태로 많이 써요.

phrases.example: 매일 집과 회사만 오가는 무미건조한 생활이 지겨워요.
phrases.en: I'm tired of a dull life of just going between home and work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 변화나 즐거움이 없는 일상을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for a daily life without change or fun.

phrases.en: He said only the results in a dry, flat way.
phrases.nuance_ko: 감정 없이 딱딱하게 말하는 모습에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes speaking stiffly and without emotion.
phrases.en_equiv: to speak in a dry way

phrases.example: 그 영화는 너무 재미없어서 중간에 나왔어요.
phrases.en: That movie was so boring that I left halfway.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요. '무미건조하다'는 더 딱딱해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simple everyday word; 무미건조하다 is more formal.

explain_en: Describes life or writing lacking interest or feeling; written style. Use it when speech, writing or life has no feeling or fun. It sounds more formal than '재미없다', so it shows up more in writing and presentations. It is often used as '무미건조한 + noun' or '무미건조하게 + verb'.

t90.ax: My daily life feels dull these days.

examples.en: I hung a picture on the white wall.

examples.ko: 이 방은 전체가 백색으로 칠해져 있어요.
examples.en: This whole room is painted white.
White powder was left at the bottom of the cup.

examples.ko: 눈이 오자 거리가 온통 백색이 되었어요.
examples.en: When it snowed, the street turned completely white.

examples.ko: 아이가 백색을 좋아해서 흰 옷만 골라요.
examples.en: My child likes white and only picks white clothes.

examples.ko: 이 컵은 백색인데 저 컵은 파란색이에요.
examples.en: This cup is white, but that cup is blue.

explain: 백색은 한자어라서 글이나 설명에서 쓰고, 일상 대화에서는 '흰색'이나 '하얀색'이라고 해요. '백색 가전', '백색 소음'처럼 굳은 말 안에서는 백색이 그대로 나와요.

phrases.en: I often wear white shirts.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '백색'보다 '흰색'을 훨씬 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily conversation, 흰색 is used far more than 백색.

phrases.en: A white cat is sitting by the window.
phrases.nuance_ko: '하얀색'은 부드럽고 친근한 느낌이 있는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: 하얀색 has a soft, friendly feel.

phrases.example: 백색 소음을 들으면 잠이 잘 와요.
phrases.en: I fall asleep well when I listen to white noise.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이 표현에서는 '흰색'이 아니라 '백색'을 그대로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In this fixed expression, 백색 is used instead of 흰색.

explain_en: White — Sino-Korean, formal or technical (백색 소음) Baeksaek is a Sino-Korean word used in writing and explanations; in everyday talk people say 'huinsaek' or 'hayansaek'. It stays as is in fixed terms like 'baeksaek gajeon' (white goods) and 'baeksaek soeum' (white noise).

p.n: 흰색 is more everyday; 백색 sounds formal or technical.

t90.ax: This whole room is painted white.

examples.ko: 화장을 지우니 얼굴 본바탕이 그대로 보여요.
examples.en: When I wash off my makeup, my natural face shows through.
A person's true nature shows when times are hard.

examples.ko: 그 친구는 본바탕이 착해서 미워할 수가 없어요.
examples.en: That friend is good-natured at heart, so I can't hate him.
I think you should look at the essence rather than the appearance.

examples.ko: 이 색은 제 얼굴 본바탕과 잘 어울려요.
examples.en: This color suits the natural look of my face well.
No matter how much you dress up, the underlying nature doesn't change.

explain: 꾸미거나 손대기 전의 원래 모습이나 타고난 성질이에요. '본성'은 성격에 쓰지만 '본바탕'은 얼굴, 재료, 사람됨에도 폭넓게 써요. '본바탕이 좋다/착하다'처럼 자주 말해요.

phrases.example: 그 친구는 본바탕이 좋아서 금방 배워요.
phrases.en: That friend has a good nature, so he learns quickly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 타고난 성질이나 바탕이 좋다고 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to praise someone's good innate nature.

phrases.en: His words are rough, but he is kind at heart.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습과 달리 속은 어떤지 말할 때 '본바탕은'으로 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used as '본바탕은' to contrast the surface with the inside.

phrases.example: 어려운 일이 생기면 사람은 본바탕을 드러내요.
phrases.en: When hard times come, people show their true nature.
phrases.nuance_ko: 감춰져 있던 원래 모습이 나타난다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the hidden original nature comes out.

explain_en: It means the original look or inborn quality before anything is added or changed. '본성' is for personality, but '본바탕' also covers faces, materials and character. It is often used like '본바탕이 좋다/착하다'.

t90.ax: A person's true nature shows when times are hard.

examples.ko: 이번 봄에는 산호색 립스틱이 정말 유행이에요.
examples.en: Coral-colored lipstick is really in fashion this spring.
My younger sister came out wearing a coral-colored dress.
After I painted the wall coral, the room became brighter.

examples.ko: 이 립밤은 산호색이라서 얼굴이 화사해 보여요.
examples.en: This lip balm is coral, so it makes your face look bright.
How are coral and pink different?

examples.ko: 바다 속 산호처럼 예쁜 산호색 가방을 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a pretty coral-colored bag, like the coral under the sea.

explain: 분홍보다 주황 느낌이 조금 더 날 때 써요. 옷이나 화장품 색 이름으로 자주 나오고, 같은 색을 '코랄'이라고도 말해요.

phrases.en: I bought a coral-colored bag.
phrases.nuance_ko: '산호색'과 같은 색인데 외래어라 옷이나 화장품 가게에서 더 자주 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: The same color as '산호색', but this loanword is heard more in clothing and cosmetics shops.

phrases.en: This skirt is coral-colored.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건의 색을 설명할 때 쓰는 기본 문장이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic sentence for describing an item's color.

phrases.en: I painted the wall coral.
phrases.nuance_ko: 색을 골라 칠하거나 바꿀 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase for choosing or changing to a color when painting.

explain_en: It is used when a color looks a bit more orange than pink. It often appears as a color name for clothes and cosmetics, and people also call the same color '코랄' (coral).

examples.ko: 그 친구는 처음 만나면 좀 새침해요.
examples.en: That friend seems a bit aloof when you first meet her.
She looked at me with a prim expression.
Why are you sitting there so primly?

examples.ko: 새침해서 말을 걸기 어려운 줄 알았어요.
examples.en: I thought she was aloof and hard to talk to.
The kid who used to be standoffish has become much brighter lately.
Don't be so stuck-up, come play with us.

explain: 쌀쌀맞게 보이고 모른 척하는 듯한 태도를 말해요. 얌전하고 도도한 척하는 느낌이라 '새침한 표정', '새침하게 굴다'처럼 많이 써요. 사람을 직접 평가하는 말이라 듣는 사람에 따라 기분이 상할 수 있어요.

phrases.en: She answered with a coy expression.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에 붙이는 활용형으로 얼굴 표정이나 목소리에 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form, often used for expressions or voices.

phrases.example: 처음 보는 사람 앞에서 새침하게 굴어요.
phrases.en: She acts coy in front of people she meets for the first time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그런 태도로 행동한다는 뜻으로 '새침하게 굴다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means to behave in that aloof way.

phrases.en: When you get to know her, she isn't coy; she's kind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 겉보기와 다르다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, used to say someone is not as they seem.

explain_en: It describes an attitude that looks cool and as if pretending not to notice. It has a demure, slightly haughty feel and is often used as '새침한 표정' or '새침하게 굴다'. Since it judges a person directly, it may offend some listeners.

examples.ko: 새 제품의 안전성에 대해 소비자들이 의문을 제기하고 있어요.
examples.en: Consumers are raising questions about the safety of the new product.

examples.ko: 차를 고를 때 첫째는 가격이고 둘째로는 안전성을 봤어요.
examples.en: When choosing a car, price came first and safety second.
This toy passed the safety inspection.

examples.ko: 약은 효과도 중요하지만 안전성이 더 중요해요.
examples.en: Effectiveness matters for medicine, but safety matters even more.

examples.ko: 아이 카시트는 무엇보다 안전성이 가장 중요해요.
examples.en: For a child's car seat, safety is the most important thing.
They say they will delay sales until the safety is confirmed.

explain: 제품, 약, 기술, 시설이 얼마나 안전한지 평가할 때 써요. 사람이나 장소가 안전할 때는 그냥 '안전해요'라고 말해요. 반대말은 '위험성'이에요.

phrases.example: 이 약은 안전성이 높다고 알려져 있어요.
phrases.en: This medicine is known to be very safe.
phrases.nuance_ko: 제품이나 약이 믿을 만큼 안전할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a product or drug is reliably safe.

phrases.en: I checked the product's safety before buying it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사용하기 전에 위험이 없는지 알아볼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when checking for risks before use.

phrases.en: The new toy passed the safety test.
phrases.nuance_ko: 제품이 안전한지 공식적으로 시험하는 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to an official test of whether a product is safe.

explain_en: It is used when evaluating how safe a product, medicine, technology or facility is. For a person or place, people simply say '안전해요'. The opposite is '위험성' (riskiness).

t90.ax: This toy passed the safety inspection.

examples.en: Colorful balloons floated into the sky.

examples.ko: 오색 한복을 입은 아이들이 춤을 춰요.
examples.en: Children in colorful hanbok are dancing.
Multicolored autumn leaves dyed the mountain.
The fireworks painted the night sky in many colors.

examples.ko: 저녁 하늘에 오색 구름이 떠 있었어요.
examples.en: Colorful clouds floated in the evening sky.
The market was full of vegetables of every color.

explain: 원래는 파랑·노랑·빨강·하양·검정의 다섯 색이에요. 한국 전통에서는 '오방색'이라고 해요. 일상에서는 숫자 5보다 '여러 가지 화려한 색'이라는 느낌으로 써서 '오색 단풍', '오색찬란하다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: The autumn mountain is covered in multicolored leaves.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빨강, 노랑 등 여러 색으로 물든 단풍을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for autumn leaves turned many colors, like red and yellow.

phrases.en: We hung multicolored balloons at the birthday party.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 가지 색의 풍선이라는 뜻이에요. 잔치나 파티 이야기에 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means balloons in many colors; fits talk about parties and celebrations.

phrases.en: Dazzling, multicolored lights came on at night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 색이 화려하고 눈부시게 빛난다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means many colors shining brilliantly and splendidly.

explain_en: Five colors, often festive or traditional, like colorful balloons. Originally it means the five colors blue, yellow, red, white and black, called '오방색' in Korean tradition. In daily use it feels like 'many splendid colors' rather than the number five, as in '오색 단풍' and '오색찬란하다'.

examples.en: The house is small, but it's livable as it is.
The pay is low, but I'm reasonably satisfied.
The food was passable.
It's okay as it is, so just use it.
Office life is tolerable as it is.

examples.ko: 이런대로 시작해 보고 나중에 고치면 돼요.
examples.en: Let's start as it is and fix it later.

explain: 완벽하지는 않아도 지금 상태로 그럭저럭 괜찮다는 뜻이에요. '그런대로'도 비슷하게 쓰는데, 이런대로는 지금 눈앞에 있는 상황이나 물건을 가리키는 느낌이 더 강해요. 뒤에 '살 만하다', '괜찮다', '먹을 만하다' 같은 말이 자주 와요.

phrases.en: The taste is okay as it is.
phrases.nuance_ko: 완벽하지 않아도 이 정도면 나쁘지 않다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means it's not perfect but not bad as it is.

phrases.en: The food is edible as it is.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식이 기대보다 못해도 먹을 수는 있을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when food falls short but is still edible.

phrases.en: The room is small, but I can get by in it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 말한 상황을 가리키는 말이라 이런대로보다 더 널리 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to an already-mentioned situation; used more widely than 이런대로.

explain_en: It means that although not perfect, it's acceptably fine in its current state. '그런대로' is used similarly, but '이런대로' feels more like pointing to the situation or thing right in front of you. It is often followed by phrases like '살 만하다', '괜찮다' and '먹을 만하다'.

en: to be playful; to be mischievous (lighthearted)

examples.en: My younger sibling has a playful expression.
That child gave a mischievous smile.
I said it playfully, but they took it seriously.
I was in a good mood today, so I felt playful.
Even though he looks playful, he's a serious friend inside.
Her voice is playful and cute.

explain: '장난'에 '-스럽다'가 붙어서 장난치는 듯한 분위기나 태도를 말해요. 진지하지 않다는 느낌이 들 수 있지만 보통은 귀엽고 밝은 쪽이에요. 심하게 짓궂으면 '짓궂다'를 써요.

phrases.en: The child laughed with a playful expression.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸밀 때 쓰는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form used to modify a noun that follows.

phrases.en: My younger sibling has a playful way of talking.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해요체 기본형으로 문장 끝에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite sentence-ending form.

phrases.en: That friend isn't playful today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 평소와 달리 진지할 때 부정형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, used when someone is serious rather than playful.

explain_en: 장난 plus -스럽다 describes an attitude or mood that seems like joking around. It can suggest not being serious, but usually in a cute, light way. For truly teasing behavior, 짓궂다 is the better word.

en: to get along with; to go with

examples.ko: 이 색과 저 색이 잘 조화돼요.
examples.en: This color and that color go well together.
The building that blends tradition and modernity looks great.
When the two flavors blend well, it tastes better.
The clothes and bag didn't match, so I changed them.
I saw an ad where the music and video work together.

examples.ko: 팀원들의 의견이 조화될 때까지 회의를 했어요.
examples.en: We kept meeting until the team members' opinions came together.

explain: '어울리다'는 사람·옷·음식에 두루 쓰는 말이고, 조화되다는 둘 이상이 부딪치지 않고 하나로 균형을 이룰 때 써요. '~와/과 조화되다', '조화된 ~'로 쓰고, 어울리다보다 글에서 더 자주 보여요.

phrases.example: 이 두 색은 잘 조화되지 않아요.
phrases.en: These two colors don't go well together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 둘이 잘 맞지 않고 따로 노는 느낌을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form says two things clash or don't blend.

phrases.en: The music goes well with the video, so the mood is nice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무엇과 조화되는지 '~와/과'로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '~와/과' to say what something harmonizes with.

phrases.en: I want to live in a house in harmony with nature.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤의 명사를 꾸며서 균형 잡힌 모습을 나타내며 글에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Modifies a noun to show a balanced look; common in writing.

explain_en: '어울리다' (suit/go with) is used broadly for people, clothes, and food; 조화되다 is for two or more things balancing into one without clashing. It is used as '~와/과 조화되다' or '조화된 ~', and shows up more in writing than 어울리다.
